_comment: OPERATOR ground truth — written from the deployment owner's stated intent (2026-07-12), independent of tags/resolver rules. Divergences vs the resolver are true semantic findings, not tautologies. See docs/BENCHMARK-RECALL.md.

_operator_notes.ensure_safety: 10 lights + alarm + notifier. The bridged media players and the bridged light must NOT act in an emergency (the operator's explicit exclusion: they are display-capable but excluded by preference).
_operator_notes.alert_anomaly: Notify; consult the motion and climate sensors and the bridged binary sensors. The bridged housekeeping and solar sensors are not wanted in this deployment (another deployment may declare otherwise).
_operator_notes.control_access: No locks in this deployment — nothing acts.
_operator_notes.notify: Notifier only. The bridged media players have no role here.
_operator_notes._pir_note: The motion sensor IS included where relevant (reading it in an emergency is useful): this operator has one and wants it read. A deployment without one simply would not register it.

_provenance.author: the deployment owner
_provenance.written: before the resolver redesign, from what the owner wants to happen — not from the tags the resolver reads
_provenance.criterion: An emergency is answered by acting; an alert is answered by detecting. Sensors are expected in alert_anomaly and report_status, and in neither ensure_safety, control_access nor notify.
_provenance.why_this_matters: This file is the only criterion here that a resolver change cannot invalidate, because it was not derived from the resolver's own tags. The 0.994 the paper reported for production was circular for exactly that reason. Five design decisions have now been settled against this file; it was re-read and confirmed rather than assumed.
_provenance.limit: Still one person. Two ground truths by the same author are not two raters, and no amount of solo work fixes that.
